content.title: Response
content.comment:
After reading the authors' response, my concerns remained.
1. For Contribution 1, I think the visualization is just to show the intermediate results of the method, and it seems a stretch to provide the interpretability for I2I style transfer. In addition, I think that for I2I translation task, I would care more about the trade-off between style rendering and semantic preservation rather than visualization. As a result, to my knowledge, it is not good to change the contribution in the revised revision.
2. Some of my concerns have not been addressed:
-From the comparison results with state-of-the-art methods, why did the author not explain the reason for the bad results mentioned in weakness 2 but replace them with other samples?
-Insufficient ablation study. Why is the content feature c1 only imposed to set_6, not to set_4 or set_5? Further, could the method reduce the number of sets, such as 9 sets? I think the ablation study should be given to justify the rationality of the proposed method.
-For the control factor Φ, although the author explained that artificially setting different values can control the trade-off between structure and texture, for the training of the network, I think this design is too subjective and laborious. Because when compared with other methods, an optimal Φ, i.e., the best trade-off, is still needed. Additionally, in different scenes, is the value of Φ fixed?

content.title: Thank you for your comments
content.comment:
Dear Reviewer 1j63:

We are grateful for your thorough review and for pointing out the potential issues in the draft. We are glad that you find our research an interesting topic, and would like to address your concerns in the following:

Weakness1: Yes, we need to have a more detailed illustration on our model structure and explain why we divide the time steps T into 11 sets (groups). We have added this information after the second paragraph of Section 3 and give a new Figure 2 of our structure and detailed caption to help readers to understand our method.

Weakness2: Yes, we missed an indication of the size of each set and did not give a detailed discussion of the effect with different Control Factor \phi. We give a detailed size of each set in Section 4. Due to the page limitation, we make a specific discussion of \phi in Appendix B.

Weakness3: Thank you for your remind of the ‘two types of set’ which could lead to confusion. We have modified this part with a new metric (Unifying Structure and Texture Similarity, DISTS) to help demonstrate the effect of feature targets and discuss the difference of different sets in our progressive style rendering (Section 4.2), which is clearer and more intuitive.

Weakness4: Thank you for your suggestions on the novelty claim. We have modify this the abstract, introduction and conclusion to emphasize the novelty and contribution of our work. Specifically, although some impressive methods (style-GAN, cycleGAN or StyTr2, etc. ) are capable of obtaining image-to-image style transfer, they lack interpretability, which means that we have no idea with the intermediate steps before the final generated images due to black box issue. Our methods can visualize these intermediate steps and let AI model imitate the painting process of artists, which provide more interpretability in the task of image-to-image translation. Moreover, existing work based on the structure of classic diffusion model cannot implement a true sense of style transfer. Although some diffusion based work make efforts by imposing the guidance on the generation process, no work can transfer the image to another artistic style while extraordinary preserving the semantic structure. Our method is totally different from the existing diffusion-based work in the structure, we design the double-ended inputs from two domains which successfully combine the necessary features and output the stylistic images in the midst layer. To the best of our knowledge, leveraging this novel structure, we are the first to successfully implement I2I style transfer with diffusion model.

Weakness5: Yes, we missed the quantitative data analysis and user study when compared with other methods. To better illustrate the performance of our method, we have added the quantitative comparison by utilizing the metric (Unifying Structure and Texture Similarity, DISTS) in Section 4.1. In Section 4.2, we use the DISTS value to make a detailed analysis of our progressive style transfer. We also conduct the user study in these days and describe in detail in Section 4.3.

Weakness6: thank you for your suggestion on the \cap structure issue. To help understand, we give a new Figure 2 of our model and design in U shape that is more intuitive, which means the deeper the set in the 'U' shaped structure the more feature targets will be imposed. Detailed description of this structrue is illustrated in the third paragraph of Section 3 and the caption of Figure 2.

Thank you again for your detailed and comprehensive comments, which have been worthwhile for our work.

content.title: Thanks for your comments
content.comment:
Dear Reviewer t82C: 

We are grateful for your thorough review and for pointing out the potential issues in the draft and thank you for your confirmation on the contribution of our work and mathematical work. We would like to address your concerns in the following:

Weakness1: Thank you for your concerns on this and your helpful suggestion reminds us to emphasis our novelty and contribution in the abstract, introduction and conclusion part in our new revision. The existing work based on the structure of classic diffusion model cannot well implement dual domain image transfer, which means that current diffusion-based models are mostly dealing with tasks such as image generation, image segmentation, super-resolution, etc. Although many improvements have been made such as impose the guidance during the generation process, they cannot achieve a true sense of style transfer given a content image and artistic style image change. To the best of our knowledge, our new structure with double-ended inputs from two domains is the first work to implement I2I style transfer with diffusion model. On the other hand, some other generative models (such as GAN, CNN based work) are capable of rendering in specific artistic styles, not enough is known about how computers painting images due to the black box problem. By utilizing diffusion model for image style transfer, for the first time, we implemented a step-by-step process to provide the interpretability for image style transfer. 

Weakness2: Thank you for your suggestions on sufficient data analysis. We have used the new metric (Unifying Structure and Texture Similarity, DISTS) to implement the quantitative evaluation in our work. We compared our work with other methods with quantitative data analysis and conduct the user study to illustrate the performance of our method. When collating the results of the questionnaire we found that, due to the subjective nature of the questionnaire, the preferences of individual people varied.

Weakness3: Yes, we need to give a detailed description of our method, we add this information after the second paragraph of Section 3. And we make a quantitative analysis of different sets in Section 4.2. Due to the page limitation, we analysis the effect of Control Factor in Appendix B and give a detailed discussion.

Weakness4: Yes, preserving semantic structure and deep style transfer cannot be obtained at the same time. We discuss this issue in Section 4.2 in our new revision. Actually, leveraging the benefit of diffusion model, we can choose the image we need from different set by our needs. If we require the result sharper in semantic structure, we can select the image in set_6; if we want to have a more stylistic image with relatively less requirement in semantic structure, we can select the image from set_5. Similarly, due to subjectivity, some people will prefer clear content when selecting results, and some may prefer more stylised ones (in the user study we found that for artistic renderings of abstract paintings, art workers preferred output images with small \phi values, their reasoning being that the symbolism of the content was more pronounced in such images).

Thank you again for your constructive suggestions on our work, which have made a crucial difference.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
The diffusion model has recently achieved excellent results in the field of generation, but in principle, it can only handle single-domain image problems, and the information between two domains cannot be efficiently combined. In this paper, the author proposed a two-domain input structure with double-ended diffusion named D3PSR to solve the image-to-image style translate problem.
1. D3PSR uses the image inputs of two domains, extracts the output in the middle step of the model as the output image of the style domain and content domain, and uses KL scatter loss to constrain the similarity with the two input images.
2. D3PSR additionally use two convolution neural networks as the style and content encoders of the images, and use KL scatter loss to constrain the style and content of the current image to be similar to the content of one input image and the style of the other input image.
Experiments show that D3PSR can effectively mix the style and image of both domains.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
+ This paper proposes a novel diffusion model structure to solve the translation problem of two domain image inputs.
+ explores interesting settings like control factor.
+ The validity of the method was proven by checking the intermediate results.

Weaknesses:
- Insufficient dataset and benchmark. It may be useful to add, for example, MS-COCO and WikiArt datasets or to indicate the dataset information already used.
- The description of the specific structure of the network is not intuitive and clear. It may be useful to describe network structure details after the second paragraph of Part 3.
- Insufficient comparison with other methods. For example, the comparison with StyTr2, StyleFormer, AdaAttn and other methods does not have enough data and analysis of details.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This paper is well-written, although some sentences have some errors. E.g., in the line 6 of Appendix “Given data xA, xB sampled from the true data distribution p_d (x_a), p_d (x_a)”, maybe the second p_d (x_a) should be p_d (x_b)?

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes an image-to-image style transfer method based on the diffusion model. The style transfer result is obtained in the midst step of the process from the image domain to the style domain. To preserve both the semantic content and the reference style, the method is designed as a double-end input '∩' shape architecture to integrate the feature between two domains and impose them progressively in different steps. Experimental results show this method can achieve progressive style rendering while preserving the main semantic structure of the source image.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths
+ The paper leverages the diffusion model to achieve image-to-image style transfer.
+ The method provides a progressive style rendering that can visualize the rendering process of stylized textures step by step.
+ The authors give a detailed mathematical basis for their method.

Weaknesses
- The novelty of this paper is limited. According to my understanding, the proposed method integrates the feature extraction of two domains into the classical diffusion model, which seems to be a minor improvement.
- Experiments are insufficient to validate the superiority of the proposed method. First, as seen in Figure 6, the results of the proposed method may not be consistent with the style reference (see colors in scenes 2, 4). Compared with StyTr, the proposed method suffers an overflow issue around object boundaries (see scenes 1, 3). Moreover, the stylized result of scene 4 may present background clutters. This issue can also be observed in Figure 4 (see the 1st, 3rd, 4th and 5th columns of scenes 3 and 5, 3rd, 4th, and 5th columns of scene 4). Second, the authors did not provide quantitative comparisons with state-of-the-art methods. I suggest adding comparisons in terms of style loss, content loss, and user preference study for further validation. 
- Some important components of the method are confusing. Why does the method choose 11 sets? How does the other number of sets affect method performance? Furthermore, as shown in Figure 8, Tables 1 and 2, the results on set_4, set_5, and set_6 are very similar. Does this mean many layers or sets are unnecessary, and why is content feature c1 imposed to set_6, not to set_4 or set_5? I think ablation study should be given to justify the rationality of the proposed method. Additionally, the control factor in the loss function is proposed to control the trade-off between structure and texture. How are the manual adjustments when choosing the values to ensure the best compromise? Are the values different for different scenes? I think this design may not accurate enough. Moreover, the authors do not give specific control factor values. 
- Some other questions. For different painting styles, such as more abstract styles, whether preserving semantic structure affect the result of style transfer? Somehow like adding a constraint? Besides, I’m curious about the output between Domain B and the midst layer, like set_9 shown in Figure 2.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- Clarity. This paper is well-organized and easy to follow.
- Quality. The author gives the necessary theoretical basis of the method. However, the rationality of some important components needs further experimental evaluation.
- Novelty. The paper attempts to use the diffusion model for style transfer, but I think the improvement is limited.
- Reproducibility. The paper does not include sufficient information about the design of the network.
content.summary_of_the_review: My concerns mainly rely on the novelty and the results of the method. In my opinion, this paper appears to be a visual model that uses the diffusion model to visualize the process of style transfer. The improvement on the classical diffusion model seems limited. More importantly, the superiority and rationality of the method lack sufficient support from the current experimental results. For the above reasons, my initial suggestion is borderline reject.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
•	The focus of the paper is to propose a method for I2I style transfer, which can preserve the semantic structure from the source image and render with the texture from the style image
•	The basic idea is to use the diffusion model to create chain of immediate results for the target and for each style. In the paper, a total of 5 styles are used.
•	Style transfer is achieved by tapping into the middle layers of the two streams to construct the final style transferred image using a loss function. 
•	The loss function consist of three terms, 1) a dual loss function which consists of a content loss and a style loss, both of which are evaluated using KL divergence, 2) a loss term to the content using data from the middle and 3) a loss term to the style using data from the middle.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
•	Using the diffusion model is an interesting idea
•	Results are interesting
•	Having several hyperparameters that a user can control the output is useful.
Weaknesses:
•	The writing of the paper is at times confusing. For example, it is unclear of the significance of the \cap architecture. No detail is included in the paper.
•	The rationale of dividing the sequence of intermediate results into 11 sets is not provided. 
•	No ablation studies are provided for \mu and \lambda, and the size of each set. In fact, their values are not provided in the paper (unless I missed them).
•	Using different sets and varying \phi appear to have a similar effect. However, there is no discussion on this issue. 
•	It appears that there are two types of sets (Table 1 and 2), one for style and one for content. But in the paper, they are regarded  to be the same, which is quite confusing.
•	There is insufficient discussion of the novelty of the proposed method, e.g. what the proposed method can do that other recently proposed style transfer methods cannot do? For example, in Fig. 6, the only discussion is one single sentence on p. 5 stating that the proposed method preserve the semantic structure of the content image and simulate the strokes of the style image from the style domain. Such a statement, which is quite generic, can be easily applied to other style transfer methods.
•	There is no quantitative comparison, e.g. style loss, user study, and efficiency, between the proposed method and other methods. 
•	One issue not discussed is the importance of using the diffusion model. What can it provide to  style transfer that no other methods can?
•	There are some occasional typos and grammatical mistakes.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity:
The writing of the paper is confusing. Some of the issues are discussed in the weaknesses above. Other than not been done before, the motivation of using the diffusion model is lacking. The description of "sets" is very confusing. To avoid such confusion, a more formal description is warranted. The significance of the \cap structure is unclear. Does that structure have to be drawn like a \cap or is it just an illustration? I fail to understand its significance even after reading the paper many times!
Quality:
Style transfer has been an active research topic for many decades, even before the advent of deep learning. While the proposed method demonstrates its ability of transfer the style from the source to the target image, it fails to demonstrate what it can do that other recent method fail. In particular, there is no user study or quantitative comparisons.
Novelty:
While using the diffusion model to to style transfer may be novel, the experimental results do not appear to support that the proposed method can produce results that other methods cannot. For example, in  Continuous and Diverse Image-to-Image Translation via Signed Attribute Vectors (IJCV 2022), to name a few, more diverse results are shown.
content.summary_of_the_review: In summary, because the writing of the paper is confusing and the experimental results are not convincing, I am not in favor of accepting the paper.

content.title: Dual-Domain Diffusion Based Progressive Style Rendering towards Semantic Structure Preservation
content.abstract: In this paper, we propose a Dual-Domain Diffusion based Progressive Style Rendering (D3PSR) method to achieve style rendering from the semantic Domain A to the style Domain B. Different from the classic diffusion models, our model takes two unpaired images from two domains as inputs, and the output is obtained at the midst layer. With the benefits from diffusion models, a dynamic rendering process was leveraged to progressively incorporate the texture strokes from the style domain while preserving the semantic structure in the noise-adding steps. Our experiments shows that a range of artistic styles can be successfully transferred into the target images without breaking their semantic structures, demonstrating the merits of our new diffusion-based approach with beyond the state-of-the-art performance in style transferring. A further study utilized the similarity scores to measure such a diffusion-based process, showing how semantic structures were rendered in our progressive process in a quantitative view.
